dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Lorraine. City Hall's closed for the day, but I can take your report.

Yeah, hi, Lorraine. Thanks. I know it's after five, I saw the message say to use this line for drains. So, um, my name's Rui Costa, I manage a few buildings up on the Hill, and I'm calling about a storm drain in front of one of them.
Okay, Mr. Costa. What's the address?

380 Pelham Street. Historic Hill, up past where the, uh, you know, the little corner market is. Which, funny thing, the owner of that building, not the market, the one I manage, she wanted to repaint the whole front door this spring, and I said wait till the street dries out, because the whole thing, anyway. The drain.
380 Pelham Street. And what's the drain doing?

It's gurgling. Like actually making noise, bubbling, and there's a sewer smell coming up out of it. Real strong, you walk by and it hits you. And this is after the rain that ended Saturday, three days ago. So it's not like it's still raining. It should've cleared.
Gurgling and a sewer smell, three days after the rain stopped. Is there water standing around it, or is it just the noise and the smell?

Okay, so the sidewalk is a sheet of mud and grit. Just coated. Sand and silt and leaves, like the whole thing washed down the hill and parked itself in front of my building. Tenants are tracking it in the hallway. I've swept it twice. Twice! It's still there.
So the sidewalk's covered in mud and grit, and you've swept it a couple times already.

Yeah. And I mean, my cousin has a place over in the Fifth Ward and he says his street was flooding too, like the whole corner, but that's his thing, I'm not calling about that. I'm just saying it's everywhere, I guess. Anyway, mine.
Understood, just yours at 380 Pelham. Has the drain been cleaned recently that you know of?

That's what I want to know. When did they last come by? Because I've been managing this building going on four years and I have never once seen a truck on this block. Not once. So when was it last cleaned? Is there a record or something?
I don't have the cleaning schedule in front of me on this line. I'll note that you're asking for the last service date for that drain, and I'll have the supervisor look it up and get back to you.
Okay. Good. Because every time it rains hard it's the same thing, and nobody comes. I'm tired of sweeping the city's mess off my sidewalk.
I hear you. Let me get a callback number so someone can reach you.

Sure, it's 401-555-0199. But, heads up, my voicemail is full. I keep meaning to clear it out, and I've tried, I pressed some buttons the other day and it just played everything back at me, a message from, I don't even know, last October. I haven't figured out how to delete them.
Okay, so 401-555-0199, and the voicemail may not take a message. Is there a better time to catch you live?
Mornings. I'm usually in my truck between buildings but I pick up. Anytime before noon is good.

Mornings, before noon. Let me read this back. Storm drain at 380 Pelham Street, gurgling, sewer odor, sidewalk covered in mud and grit since the rain that ended Saturday, and you want to know when it was last cleaned. Did I get that right?
Yep, that's it. And the smell, please put the smell. That's what the tenants keep complaining about.
Smell's in there. I'll send it to the crew supervisor tonight so it's in front of them first thing tomorrow.
Okay. I appreciate it. I just want somebody to actually come look this time.
I understand. Someone will call you, and if you don't pick up, they'll likely try again, so keep an ear out in the morning.
Will do. Thanks, Lorraine.
You're welcome, Mr. Costa. Have a good evening.
